review_evidence: Reviewed the 299-file pinned snapshot and formal-mathfin architecture/status documentation.

The library contains hundreds of machine-checked mathematical-finance theorems spanning FTAP, stochastic calculus, Black-Scholes, Feynman-Kac, Girsanov, martingale representation, risk measures, and related foundations.
Test and upstream Lean files remain potentially useful formal examples/dependencies; no source-local lossless exclusion was established.
summary: Retain formal-mathfin as a large substantive Lean mathematical-finance formalization.

review_evidence: Declaration grep (theorem|lemma|def|structure|class|instance|inductive|abbrev|example|axiom at line start) over all 269 files: 267 match; MathFin.lean and lakefile.lean do not.

MathFin.lean (26512 bytes): 285 import lines plus a module docstring describing the library layout; umbrella module, retained as navigation under FILTER-007 (no end-to-end auxiliary delivery verified).

lakefile.lean: Lake package config with comments documenting the Challenge/Solution Comparator contract, AxiomAudit build harness, and BrownianMotion/mathlib pins; retained as project interface documentation.

Challenge.lean read completely: ADEH coherent-risk-measure structure IsCoherentRisk, def representingSet, theorems coherentRisk_isLUB and worstCase_isCoherentRisk stated with sorry (Comparator statement of record) plus a long mathematical docstring.
Solution.lean read completely: repeats the ADEH declarations and proves them from MathFin.coherentRisk_isLUB and MathFin.worstCase_isCoherent.

MathFin/AxiomAudit.lean (87537 bytes, largest) and MathFin/AxiomAuditGen.lean (78348 bytes, generated): headers read; bodies are #guard_msgs-pinned #print axioms checks of MathFin theorems with narrative sections; no declarations, but they are build-enforced axiom certificates naming the library's theorems, so retained under FILTER-002 as downranking candidates rather than hard-excluded.

Largest proof files (Foundations/GirsanovPredictableTheta.lean 71514, DoobLpMaximalInequality.lean 60538, GirsanovAdaptedTheta.lean 49333, PointwiseBracket.lean 40044) contain theorem/def declarations.
Smallest AmericanPut file MathFin/BlackScholes/AmericanPut/Boundary/DividendContact.lean (1596 bytes) read: theorem contact_iff with full tactic proof for the dividend put boundary.

grep -lw sorry over the list: hits in Challenge.lean (intended), the audit files and lakefile (comments), and five Foundations files (word occurrences to be expected in docstrings/comments of a sorry-free library per AxiomAudit); none is grounds for exclusion.
Directory listings of MathFin/Contracts and MathFin/Execution show topical modules (Adapted, CappedCall, Pricing, GlostenMilgrom) with declarations.
scripts/zz_necessity_batch.lean (77 bytes) read completely: `import Mathlib`, `open MeasureTheory`, `example : False := by exact @MemLp.mul`.

rules.content_invariant: The file declares nothing named, states no mathematical proposition beyond the ill-typed `False` probe, and proves nothing; the only referenced constant, MemLp.mul, is owned and indexed by Mathlib.
evidence: Read all 6 lines of scripts/zz_necessity_batch.lean: `import Mathlib`, `open MeasureTheory`, `example : False := by`, `  exact @MemLp.mul`; no other content.
rules.rationale: Scratch probe script outside the MathFin library: its only command is an `example : False` whose proof term is the Mathlib lemma MemLp.mul, which does not have type False; it is a throwaway elaboration check, not a statement or proof of this repository.

summary: Surveyed all 269 listed files by directory (MathFin/BlackScholes/AmericanPut/Stopping 124, AmericanPut/Boundary 49, Foundations 57, BlackScholes 16, Contracts 5, Binomial 3, Execution 2, FixedIncome 2, Futures/Performance/RiskMeasures 1 each, root 4, scripts 1) and by size extremes. A Lean declaration grep over every file found declarations in all but MathFin.lean and lakefile.lean. I read the outliers: the root umbrella, lakefile, Challenge/Solution pair, both axiom-audit harnesses, the scripts file, and the smallest AmericanPut modules. The unit is a substantive mathematical-finance formalization (Black-Scholes, American put free boundary and optimal stopping, Ito/Girsanov foundations, risk measures) and stays searchable. The one exclusion is scripts/zz_necessity_batch.lean, a 77-byte scratch probe whose only content is an ill-typed `example : False` referencing Mathlib's MemLp.mul.
